bytecode_boundaries.description: The portable Python K semantics is source-level and must not depend on CPython bytecode opcode selection, inline-cache layout, adaptive specialization, eval-loop instruction dispatch, or compiler optimization details.

CPython disassembly, opcode tables, pseudo-instructions, inline cache metadata, adaptive bytecode display, labels, offsets, and position rendering are implementation-profile behavior sourced from dis/opcode and the generated opcode metadata.

CPython compile(), incremental compilation, AST-to-bytecode code generation, assembler behavior, stack metadata, code object attributes, and code object replacement are future CPython-profile work distinct from portable construct semantics.
The marshal format, including code-object support and version-specific compatibility constraints, is intentionally undocumented and reserved for CPython .pyc/module-cache support.

CPython .pyc file generation, invalidation modes, cache paths, sourceless bytecode loading, and importlib cache integration require a filesystem/import-cache profile rather than portable language semantics.

The CPython eval loop, adaptive specialization, inline caches, opcode dispatch, frame layout, and reference-counting/interpreter internals are implementation details outside the current source-level K semantics.

reference_runs.command: ./python -m test --single-process --timeout 240 test_dis test_compile test_codeop test_compiler_codegen test_compiler_assemble test_marshal test_py_compile test_compileall
reference_runs.result: success: all 8 CPython bytecode/compiler/cache profile tests OK
reference_runs.notes: Run against local CPython 3.14.6 source build; total bytecode-profile run reported 601 tests run, 14 skipped, all OK.

known_gaps: No K code-object value, co_* metadata surface, frame instruction pointer, or bytecode offset/source-position mapping is modeled.
No CPython opcode table, pseudo-instruction lowering, inline cache, adaptive specialization, or eval-loop dispatch is modeled.
No CPython compiler pipeline from AST to code objects, bytecode optimizer, assembler, stack effect, or code-object validation is modeled.
No marshal code-object serialization, .pyc header, invalidation mode, cache path, or sourceless loader behavior is modeled.
The current executable semantics should treat this as an implementation profile and not as evidence of portable Python language behavior.
